s: After working out a proof of concept on his laptop computer, he successfully pulled the attitude and traffic off the ADS-B receiver and began experimenting with different HUD converters. When he hooked up a 5-inch HDMI screen to the $7 cellphone reflector, it was not optimal. It had poor daylight visibility, the top of the screen was cropped off, and eyes focused in too closely at the point of reflection. He next tried a piece of teleprompter glass in a custom 3D-printed case. It was relatively inexpensive but had similar downsides as the cellphone reflector. When he got the go-ahead from his wife to buy a $215 Hudly automotive projector, he found that it worked great.
